answer: She asked me where my office was.

other_correct: She usually asked me when the bus came.
instruction_problem: Second correct order: 'usually' can go before 'asked' (She usually asked me when the bus came), which is grammatical and natural with a different meaning; a card-order checker with one key will reject it.

answer: She asked if the parcel had arrived.
He asked if the shop could deliver on Sunday.
other_correct: On Sunday he asked if the shop could deliver.
He asked on Sunday if the shop could deliver.
instruction_problem: Second correct order: 'on Sunday' can attach to 'asked' (On Sunday he asked... / He asked on Sunday if...), both grammatical and natural; the time phrase is ambiguous between the asking and the delivering.
